subject: Acme MAP: Post-call recap & proposed milestones
summary: Post-call recap confirming Acme's pain (cost, latency, observability), agreed goals, stakeholders, and an initial mutual action plan with milestones and dates.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ross <jordan.ross@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme MAP: Post-call recap & proposed milestones

Thanks for the time today, Jordan — really helpful conversation. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, stakeholders, and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP). Please confirm or correct anything I got wrong and add any missing stakeholders.

Pain points (what you told us):
- Inference unit cost is high (spiky spend during batch processing & unpredictable peak cost).
- P95 latency spikes on search ranking model during peak traffic (impacts user experience).
- Lack of token-level observability and hard to triage model regressions across environments.
- Need for stronger compliance evidence for audit (SOC2-type artifacts).

High-level goals (90-day horizon):
1) Reduce per-token inference cost ~30–40% through batching/quantization and smarter routing.
2) Stabilize p95 latency under 200ms for typical queries.
3) Deploy a private instance or VPC option to satisfy data residency and audit needs.
4) Establish monitoring and regression alerts tied to your eval prompts.

Stakeholders we heard:
- Jordan Ross — CTO / decision sponsor
- Priya Shah — Head of Infrastructure (technical approver for PoC)
- Sam Lee — Procurement (contract & purchase)
- Maya Tran — Product (primary user)

Proposed MAP (draft milestones & tentative dates):
1) 2026-07-07 — Technical demo + Q&A (Redwood -> Priya, Jordan, Maya).
2) 2026-07-09 — Security/compliance evidence pack (SOC2 artifacts, network diagram) delivered to Priya.
3) 2026-07-14 — Shortlist of recommended model configs + cost/latency projections for your workload.
4) 2026-07-21 — 2-week PoC kick-off (private trial or dedicated capacity) with defined success criteria.
5) 2026-08-04 — Procurement/contract target (aiming for signed contract).

Open items / asks for Acme:
- Please confirm the stakeholders above and add any procurement/legal contacts.
- Confirm that 7/7 for the demo works and share preferred times (PST).
- If available, share a small sample of typical query load (anonymized) to help sizing.

Attachment: Acme_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP draft with milestones and responsibilities).

Next step: I'll schedule the 7/7 demo once I get a preferred time from you — I'll include Lauren (technical lead) and Monica (CS lead) on the invite.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
From: Jordan Ross <jordan.ross@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MAP: Post-call recap & proposed milestones

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our discussion and the timeline looks achievable. A couple of clarifications: 

- Priya (cc'd) will be the technical approver for the PoC and needs the SOC2/network diagrams before the demo if possible.
- Sam (cc'd) is the procurement contact and will drive the purchase timeline; Sam, please confirm if 8/4 is reasonable for contracting.
- For the demo on 7/7, Priya and I prefer the morning window between 9-11am PST.

Also, one more ask: can you include a short note on fallback behavior and graceful degradation if the private instance gets overwhelmed? That's a showstopper risk for us.

We're happy to share an anonymized sample of query logs — I'll loop in Priya to coordinate.

Thanks — Jordan
